units.title: Classify a cubic functional equation by reciprocal normalization
units.statement: The solutions of f(x)f(y)f(x-y)=x²f(y)-y²f(x) on the real numbers are f=0 and f(x)=±x. If one nonzero value exists, all nonzero arguments have nonzero values. With g(x)=x²/f(x), the equation becomes f(x-y)=g(x)-g(y). Oddness and the substitutions y=-x,2x show g=f; therefore f is additive and f(x)²=x², forcing ± identity.
steps: Use x=y=0 to obtain f(0)=0 and rule out isolated nonzero values
Divide by f(x)f(y), derive oddness, and compare x, -x, 2x
Apply additivity and the square identity to classify the two nonzero maps
